chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from the one who narrated it, from Jameel, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so a group of people from the inhabitants of Sijistan entered upon him and asked him about the dirhams that were coated over. He said: 'There is no problem with it, provided it was a license (or permitted) in the city.'

key_terms.الْمَحْمُولِ: Coated or covered (referring to currency with a base metal core covered by silver)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using coated or debased dirhams in Islamic law?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *urf* (customary practice) in monetary transactions, ruling that coated dirhams are permissible provided they possess official validity (*jawaz*) in the specific region. This highlights the Shia juristic reliance on local economic customs and state sanction to determine the acceptability of currency, rather than relying solely on intrinsic metal value. The ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic finance in adapting to varying regional standards of trade and governance.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from the one who narrated it, from Jameel, from Hareyz Bin Abdullah who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so a group of people came over to him<sup>asws</sup> from the inhabitants of Sijistan. So they asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Dirhams coated over. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem when it was licenced (currency) in a city’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from those who narrated to him from Jamil from Hariz ibn ‘Abd Allah who has said the following:

“I once was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when a people from Sajistan came to him (the Imam) and asked about dirham with impurities. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful if they currently are in circulation in a city.’”
